The weighted average cost is calculated on a periodic basis at the end of each month. The calculation uses the total cost of goods available for sale during the month (opening stock plus purchases) divided by the total number of units available for sale. This average cost is then used to value closing stock and to determine the cost of goods sold for the month.

The Company does not use the first-in, first-out (FIFO) or last-in, first-out (LIFO) methods. The use of the weighted average method is considered to provide a fair and consistent matching of costs with revenues, particularly given the bulk purchasing patterns and the mixed nature of the stock line items.

**3. Stock Count Procedures**

A full physical stock count shall be undertaken at least once per financial year, at or near the year-end date of 31 March. The count will be planned and supervised by the Warehouse Manager, with the results recorded on pre-numbered stock count sheets. Any discrepancies between the physical count and the perpetual inventory records will be investigated and, where appropriate, adjustments will be posted to the nominal ledger after authorisation by the Finance Director.

In addition to the annual count, cyclical counts of high-value or fast-moving lines shall be conducted on a quarterly basis.

**4. Valuation of Damaged or Obsolete Stock**

Stock that is identified as damaged, obsolete, or slow-moving is written down to its net realisable value. This write-down is calculated on a line-by-line basis and is reviewed at each reporting date. The write-down is recognised as an expense in the period in which it is identified.

Adopted by special resolution on 15 January 2023.

The regulations contained in the Model Articles for Private Companies Limited by Shares (as prescribed by the Companies (Model Articles) Regulations 2008) shall apply to the company, subject to the following modifications:

1. **Directors.** The minimum number of directors shall be one and the maximum number shall be five. A director need not hold any share qualification.

2. **Borrowing Powers.** The directors may exercise all the powers of the company to borrow money, to charge its undertaking, property and uncalled capital, and to issue debentures, provided that the aggregate amount outstanding at any time shall not exceed £250,000 without the prior sanction of an ordinary resolution of the company.

3. **Retirement by Rotation.** At each annual general meeting, one-third of the directors for the time being, or, if their number is not a multiple of three, the number nearest to one-third, shall retire from office. A retiring director shall be eligible for re-election.

4. **Indemnity.** Subject to the provisions of the Companies Act 2006, every director or other officer of the company shall be indemnified out of the assets of the company against any liability incurred by him or her in that capacity.

5. **Dividends.** The directors may from time to time pay to the members such interim dividends as appear to the directors to be justified by the profits of the company which are available for distribution.

6. **Accounts.** The directors shall cause accounting records to be kept in accordance with section 386 of the Companies Act 2006, and shall cause to be prepared for each financial year such accounts as may be required by law.

7. **Financial Year.** The financial year of the company shall end on 31 March in each year, unless the directors shall otherwise determine.

Signed by the subscribers on 15 January 2023.

Hazel Margaret Whitmore
Arthur James Whitmore

The weighted average cost is calculated on a periodic basis at the end of each month. The calculation uses the total cost of goods available for sale during the month (opening stock plus purchases) divided by the total number of units available for sale. This average cost is then used to value closing stock and to determine the cost of goods sold for the month.

The Company does not use the first-in, first-out (FIFO) or last-in, first-out (LIFO) methods. The use of the weighted average method is considered to provide a fair and consistent matching of costs with revenues, particularly given the bulk purchasing patterns and the mixed nature of the stock line items.

**3. Stock Count Procedures**

A full physical stock count shall be undertaken at least once per financial year, at or near the year-end date of 31 March. The count will be planned and supervised by the Warehouse Manager, with the results recorded on pre-numbered stock count sheets. Any discrepancies between the physical count and the perpetual inventory records will be investigated and, where appropriate, adjustments will be posted to the nominal ledger after authorisation by the Finance Director.

In addition to the annual count, cyclical counts of high-value or fast-moving lines shall be conducted on a quarterly basis.

**4. Valuation of Damaged or Obsolete Stock**

Stock that is identified as damaged, obsolete, or slow-moving is written down to its net realisable value. This write-down is calculated on a line-by-line basis and is reviewed at each reporting date. The write-down is recognised as an expense in the period in which it is identified.

**5. Approval**
